title: Dạ, chào cô
englishTitle: Respectful hello to an aunt-age woman
summary: Use Dạ, chào cô when the woman feels older than chị but not elderly enough for bà.

sections.title: At a glance
sections.body: Dạ, chào cô is a respectful hello for an older woman who feels aunt-age, a teacher, a shop owner, a homestay host, or a helpful older local. It feels warmer than a generic hello because it recognizes the relationship.

sections.title: The standard way
sections.body: Use it when cô sounds more natural than chị, especially if the person is clearly older than an older-sister role.

sections.title: When to use it
sections.body: Use it with an aunt-age woman at a shop, market stall, family-run hotel, food stand, class, clinic desk, or neighborhood setting.

sections.title: Good to know
sections.body: Cô can also be used for teachers or women in a teacher-like role. That makes this phrase useful beyond literal family age.
